_doc: How each monster comes to know where the hero is (src/senses.py; Brandon, 2026-11-12: no monster knows where you are unless it is thematically and lore appropriate). Every monster sees (a real line of sight, within its perception_range, default 8) and hears (the noise the hero makes). Some have a lore sense on top, listed under 'families' (every member) and 'monsters' (one kind; it replaces the family's list). 'blind' takes sight away. Ranges are tiles. A sense that goes 'through_walls' finds the hero behind stone; 'needs_motion' fails while he stands still; 'sees_invisible' is not fooled by invisibility. 'lines' are said the first time on a floor that a kind finds him that way, when it is within 'line_reach' tiles (2026-11-12: never naming what he cannot see): 'known' when he can see it and knows the kind (family_lore.knowledge KNOWN), which teaches the sense; 'seen' when he can see it but does not know it, which shows only what it does; 'unseen' when he cannot see it, which never names it ({The} is never in it).

lines.known: {The} lifts {his} head and sniffs the air. {He} has your scent, and walls will not hide you from {him}.
lines.seen: {The} lifts {his} head, sniffs the air, and turns toward you.
lines.unseen: Somewhere close, something sniffs the air, and stops.

lines.known: {The} goes still, then turns toward you. {He} feels your footsteps through the stone; stand still and {he} loses you.
lines.seen: {The} goes very still, then turns toward you.
lines.unseen: You feel, more than hear, something shift in the stone nearby.

lines.known: A chill runs over your skin. {The} has felt the warmth of the living.
lines.seen: A chill runs over your skin as {the} turns toward you.
lines.unseen: A chill runs over your skin, as if something had noticed you.

lines.known: A thin, shrill clicking: {the} sees you with sound.
lines.seen: A thin, shrill clicking, and {the} turns your way.
lines.unseen: A thin, shrill clicking, somewhere in the dark.

lines.known: A pressure behind your eyes. {The} has felt your thoughts.
lines.seen: A pressure behind your eyes. {The} is looking at you.
lines.unseen: A pressure behind your eyes, as if something were listening.

lines.known: {The} turns, as if someone had called {his} name. The Furies always find the guilty.
lines.seen: {The} turns, as if someone had called {his} name.
lines.unseen: Somewhere, something turns, as if someone had called its name.

noise._doc: Radii in tiles, measured along open ground (sound goes round corners and through doorways, not through stone; a closed door muffles it by 'door_cost' tiles). Footsteps: 'step' at DEX 10, one tile quieter for every 'dex_per_tile' points of DEX over 10 (never below 1), 'light' tiles louder under a Light load, 'heavy' under a Heavy one, 'burdened' when Burdened and 'overloaded' when Overloaded (data/gear_rules.json load; the four tiers since 2026-11-16, when a load over half the limit was Heavy +1 and over three quarters Burdened +2), and louder in medium or heavy body armour and in metal (gear_rules.json armour_weight, gear.footstep_tiles); Cat's Footfall and silent walking make none. A monster already hunting the hero listens harder: 'hunter_bonus'. Tuned down after Brandon's play-test (2026-11-12: "a SHIT TON of monsters all descended on me at once, early on the first floor"): a fight carried 8 tiles and drew every waking creature in reach; now 5. The squeaky board rouses what is within 20 tiles of it, not the whole floor.

waking._doc: A creature asleep (not a deep sleeper of a zoo, graveyard or barracks: those have their own odds in src/sleepers.py) may wake when it hears something. 'step_near' is the chance per step heard within 'near' tiles, 'step_far' beyond that; 'loud' is for fights, doors, alarms and coin, 'loud_far' beyond half the noise's reach. The hero's DEX, Cat's Footfall, silent walking, the Hand of Glory and a heavy pack change the footstep odds as they do for the deep sleepers. A sleeper gets ONE chance to wake a turn, at the most waking noise it heard that turn (a fight is two noises a round, and two rolls made the sleepers beside it all but sure to wake).

search._doc: A creature that loses the hero goes to the last place it saw, smelled or heard him and searches there for a while ('turns', more if it was roused by an alarm or a call for help), then gives up and goes back to what it was doing. 'lost_line' is said when one the hero can see gives up.
search.lost_line: {The} loses your trail and turns away.

jobs._doc: What a creature does before it notices the hero, chosen when the floor is made (populate_floor): 'wander' roams from room to room, 'guard' keeps its post and turns to look, 'sleep' sleeps until something wakes it. Weights by family; a pack shares one job. Ambushers, mimics, rooted things, named foes and the bosses keep their own ways.

status_lines._doc: What Observe (O) says of a creature's state.
status_lines.stalking: {He} is following you, just out of reach.

sense_names.master: knowing every stone of {his} own house

scavengers._doc: C3: the things that eat the dead. An idle scavenger (not hunting, not searching, awake) that smells a corpse within 'reach' tiles goes to it and eats it in 'eat_turns' turns, healing 'heal_share' of its health; the corpse is gone, so a harvest is a race. Ghouls ate the dead in the old stories; vermin and oozes eat anything.

wanderers._doc: What the hero is told as a floor's grace runs out (src/wanderers.py; the dials are in src/floor_curve.py). Nothing new comes onto a floor while he explores it. 'warning' is said once, near the end of the grace; 'stirs' when it runs out and newcomers begin to come down the stairs, slowly at first, faster the longer he stays. A hero who leaves and comes back finds the floor settled again, and may hear both again.
warning: The floor has gone quiet, the way a held breath is quiet. You have been here a long while.
Somewhere above, something sniffs the air where you walked. You have been here a long while.
Dust sifts down from the ceiling, as if something heavy is moving on the stair. You have lingered here a long time.
stirs: Footsteps on the stair, and more behind them: word of you has spread. Things will come looking now, and keep coming while you stay.
Somewhere a door bangs open. The floor knows you are here, and more of the dungeon is coming down to see. The longer you stay, the more will come.
A horn sounds far above. The dungeon has noticed you, and newcomers will find their way down here for as long as you linger.
